title: Cinematic Homage: A Reinterpretation of Akira
content:
## **_Bridging anime imagination and grounded realism: How Soohwan Oh masters intricate leather textures and silhouettes with Marvelous Designer._**

**Discover the work and expert Marvelous Designer tips of Soohwan Oh in this exclusive series! [**[**Go to Previous Post]**](https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/4caba29455c442e1b0087639cd5190ac)

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4gnFmZIQkxk

# **You’ve recreated the legendary motorcycle sequence from the anime Akira. When translating such an intense visual into 3D, what specific aspects of the clothing’s silhouette and texture did you focus on most?**

While the project was inspired by the original Akira, my primary goal was to maximize the sense of realism, as I was reinterpreting it through a photorealistic lens. At the same time, I felt it was crucial to preserve the visceral impact of the source material. To maintain that iconic presence, I opted for a monochromatic color scheme for the outfit. Specifically, I took a cue from the protagonist’s signature red suit but reinterpreted it in a deep purple to better reflect the unique mood and atmosphere of my character.

![134ca2b379c343c29d03be4c467f207b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/134ca2b379c343c29d03be4c467f207bChasm%27s%20Call_Character_Detail_1_00000.png)

![08918f405d6e4630b5b334d41ba24a5a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/08918f405d6e4630b5b334d41ba24a5aChasm%27s%20Call_Character_Detail_1_00002.png)I designed the outfit with a sleek, form-fitting silhouette to clearly define the character’s frame. By opting for a stiff, heavy-weight leather, I was able to emphasize both structural integrity and a realistic tactile depth. To ensure the materials felt at home in a dystopian setting, I paid close attention to the weathering effects. Rather than going for an exaggerated, damaged look, I focused on achieving a sense of 'lived-in' realism—recreating the natural fading and subtle wear that comes from genuine, long-term use.

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sGJvDWgFl5Q

![8219b7f534514c96bde8306dae980a90](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/8219b7f534514c96bde8306dae980a90Chasm%27s%20Call_Character_Detail_2_psd.png)![e2f8a16244484b91ae646d27c5259c27](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/e2f8a16244484b91ae646d27c5259c27Chasm%27s%20Call_Character_Detail_1_00001_psd.png)

# **How did Marvelous Designer assist you in bridging the gap between the exaggerated wrinkles of the anime and high-end photorealistic 3D?**

If you look at the bomber jacket in the original anime, the folds aren't scattered across the entire garment; instead, the design is defined by bold, chunky wrinkles concentrated specifically around the pushed-up sleeves. While the exact material isn't explicitly defined in the anime, I reinterpreted it as a thick, heavy leather, similar to a classic rider’s jacket.

![85f108ea9bfe4600904d40f56a6d4f35](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/85f108ea9bfe4600904d40f56a6d4f35%E1%84%86%E1%85%AE%E1%86%AF%E1%84%89%E1%85%A5%E1%86%BC.png)

To achieve this in Marvelous Designer, I fine-tuned the fabric properties to suppress fine micro-folds and instead focused on emphasizing the bold, natural wrinkles created by the pushed-up sleeves. Considering the jacket’s rigid and heavy nature, I purposely increased the weight values to ensure its structural silhouette remained intact. I also dialed down the stretch and elasticity parameters to reflect the inelasticity of genuine leather, aiming for a more grounded and realistic tactile feel.

# **During the reinterpretation process, were there any specific costume details or layering strategies you introduced that reflect your own personal style, beyond what was in the original source material?**

![493708a0de7140f882f5d54fbf10a867](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/493708a0de7140f882f5d54fbf10a867Chasm%27s%20Call_Character_Detail_3.png)

![a0c98a0193d145c9a6343244e4180930](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/a0c98a0193d145c9a6343244e4180930Chasm%27s%20Call_Character_Detail_4.png)

Since the original material is an anime, I felt that translating it directly into photorealism would create some visual dissonance. For example, the protagonist's oversized jacket—with its unrealistic volume for motorcycle riding—or the iconic red cape of the villain, Tetsuo, could feel out of place in a realistic graphic setting. I believed that the process of reinterpreting these elements with a more grounded logic was key to establishing my own unique style within the project.

![29280b0b4a3642da8b9843314a532aeb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/29280b0b4a3642da8b9843314a532aebezgif-1c3d545a92f8bbf6.gif)

![ab1df06979f24559970db2e86dfd88e3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/ab1df06979f24559970db2e86dfd88e3Capture.png)For the protagonist, I reconstructed the outfit using functional, realistic garment details to ensure it looked natural for an actual rider, drawing specific inspiration from Vetements collections for the intricate details on the jacket and trousers. As for the villain, rather than sticking to the original red cape, I reinterpreted it as a red long coat to provide a more grounded and substantial feel. I crafted the overall silhouette and style in a modern, sophisticated direction, referencing Balenciaga’s lookbooks to achieve a refined, high-fashion edge.

![6b1619c7a2b14f68abfb1c77577baedc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/6b1619c7a2b14f68abfb1c77577baedcCapture%281%29.png)

![421477fbacc34b43bd4257d8891bcecc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/c613e4a3c68d49a8a1e0b49cf1592a9c/images/421477fbacc34b43bd4257d8891bceccChasm%27s%20Call_Poster_jpg.jpg)

title: Dream Sequence 3D Challenge - Seoul
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/4caba29455c442e1b0087639cd5190ac/images/3de602c15cda4cd49357397e2e650e8bDream_Sequence_StillCut.jpg)**_Step into a futuristic Seoul DJ festival where_**[** _Soohwan Oh_**](https://www.instagram.com/ohso0hwan)** _blends K-tradition and street vibes through Marvelous Designer’s intricate digital fashion!_**

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xl267-ssVEw

 _Blender – Scene building, Motion, Lighting & Rendering_

 _Marvelous Designer – Cloth Simulation & Animation_

 _Daz – Character Modeling_

 _After effects - Compositing_

# **Artist and Project Introduction**

Hello, I’m 3D artist Soohwan Oh.

Currently, I work as a freelancer, leading various visual projects primarily within the entertainment and beauty industries. I often handle the entire process—from initial planning to final production—solo, though I also participate as a supervisor or team member for larger-scale projects. As a 3D generalist, I take a hands-on approach to most stages of the creative workflow.

This project was my submission for Pwnisher’s ‘Dream Sequence’ challenge held earlier this year. The core task was to express a sense of motion synced to 120bpm music, which I chose to interpret through the theme of DJing. I wanted to make the visuals more engaging by integrating traditional Korean elements. Drawing inspiration particularly from the energy of BLACKPINK’s ‘JUMP’ music video, I worked with the vision of a DJ festival taking place in a near-future Seoul.  


YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RJ1oyLj1bXk?start=0

# **How was Marvelous Designer utilized in this project?**

Character design was pivotal for this work, as the entire scene—including camera animation, stage lighting, and fireworks—revolves around the central DJ figure. While the character wears a Hahoe mask (a traditional Korean mask) to highlight cultural roots, I also needed to convey a streetwear aesthetic that fits a modern DJ. Therefore, the core objective was to create a costume that naturally fused Korean traditional beauty with a contemporary street vibe.  
![af5324c8bd864f409286adf7141024b4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/4caba29455c442e1b0087639cd5190ac/images/af5324c8bd864f409286adf7141024b4Capture%281%29.png)Marvelous Designer was an indispensable tool throughout the detailed planning and production of these garments. Beyond standard clothing creation, it proved highly efficient for incorporating complex elements like the Gonryongpo (royal dragon robe) features and traditional Korean patchwork details.

# **What are your favorite features or tools in Marvelous Designer?**

![000dce68176b439b8969df0a47b70bd9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/4caba29455c442e1b0087639cd5190ac/images/000dce68176b439b8969df0a47b70bd9Capture%282%29.png)![0e41e67229e34b099a316382c5412617](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/4caba29455c442e1b0087639cd5190ac/images/0e41e67229e34b099a316382c5412617Capture.png) First, I frequently use ‘M:N Free Sewing.’ As garments become more complex, the sewing process can often get confusing or tricky. However, as long as you know which patterns connect to which parts, this feature allows for a fast and intuitive workflow, which is a massive help in saving production time.

Second is the ‘Attach to Measure (Avatar)’ feature. Although I didn’t use it for this specific project, it is incredibly useful for securing garments to the character. For example, simulations can sometimes become unstable when fabric is tucked inside shoes; in such cases, I use this tool to pin the cloth to the ankle area for stability. It’s also great for scenes with hanging fabrics, like curtains, where the support structure isn't visible in the camera frame. By attaching the fabric to a simple primitive, I can achieve a natural look very quickly—making it a go-to tool when I need to deliver results on a tight schedule.

![c2aa6cd51b894619a5afb4ace292b2bc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/4caba29455c442e1b0087639cd5190ac/images/c2aa6cd51b894619a5afb4ace292b2bcCapture%283%29.png)Lastly, I frequently utilize the **‘Graphic (2D Pattern)’** feature. I often create and export Diffuse maps directly within Marvelous Designer, and this tool significantly boosts my efficiency. It allows me to intuitively visualize how graphics are applied to a pattern even before the UV unwrapping stage, making the overall workflow much more streamlined.

title: USD to Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth not working properly
content:
I have some problems using the USD to Unreal Engine Chaos Cloth workflow.

I have followed the official Marvelous Designer tutorial, but noticed my outfits have this strange effect that makes them be almost completely black in the scenes, but not inside the Cloth Asset window.

![eb66b393653a44e2aeee49d9209cb186](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/2569a1d02fc74fe7825bc936ebe5805e/images/eb66b393653a44e2aeee49d9209cb186clothAssetSkeletalMesh.PNG)In the Cloth Asset editor.

![381a38a2aaae4b7e954390e5742f13bc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/2569a1d02fc74fe7825bc936ebe5805e/images/381a38a2aaae4b7e954390e5742f13bcviewportSkeletalMesh.PNG)In the viewport.

I know the best place to ask this kind of question would be in the Unreal Engine forums, but I can't seem to be able to get any help about this problem and surely there's people who have had the same problem at some point.

I could also use LiveSync, but I would end up not having any of the material properties available with a usd file.

Environment:  
\- UE 5.7  
\- Marvelous Designer Personal 2026.0.189

Thank you!
content_description: This page seeks to troubleshoot and gather community insights on resolving black outfit rendering issues when using the USD to Unreal Engine 5.7 Chaos Cloth workflow with Marvelous Designer assets.

title: Morph Target Obj Format export
content:
Hi, I've updated MD to last version, 2026.0, but now when I import object as garment, simulate end export back in obj format, when i try to import back to Daz Studio I've a warning, "Geometry did not match, failed to create morph". Never had this problem before (I've used MD for three years). Export is as always, I've positively checked Studio import making a MT with Blender, so the problem appears be in MD export.

Thanks in advance.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: I am also having this same issue, my workflow is sending from Daz > Zbrush with GoZ, then export from Zbrush as obj, importing that obj into MD, simulating, and then exporting the obj from MD. The simulation OBJ is then imported back into Daz as a morph using Morph Loader Pro. After the update, Daz says the MD objs don't match and won't import them as morphs. I tried setting a bunch of different export options from MD with no luck. I will be reverting back to the previous version until this issue is fixed.Edit: Confirmed reverting to 2025 fixes the issue for the same obj

Comment 2: Hey ErikFor this issue, it will be best if you could provide us with some more info for testing and identifying the source that is triggering that from DAZ. Please fill out a ticket at our Contact Us page, and please include:- The OBJ from the new version that is triggering the issue- The same OBJ exported from a previous versionThis way we can be sure if is a bug from the version or a corruption of the file. 🙏🏻
Reply 1: I followed the instructions and send the two obj. I can confirm that reverting back to the previous version fix the problem.
Reply 2: New version 2026.0.211 DON'T fix the problem.For my workflow I continue to use last 2025 version.Thanks
content_description: This web page provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving geometry mismatch and morph creation errors when exporting garments from Marvelous Designer 2026.0 to Daz Studio.
